item.title: Nvidia announces probe into Huang amid reports China spied on him
item.description: Chip giant Nvidia’s board announced Sunday it had opened a probe into chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang after he acknowledged an affair with a woman US officials say was working for Chinese intelligence. Late last month, The New York Times reported that US intelligence officials concluded that Alice Huang, a Chinese executive linked to a Singapore-based data center company called Megaspeed, had been funnelling information to Beijing. The executive, also known as Huang Le, and no relation to 63-year-old Taiwanese-born Jensen Huang, developed a close relationship with the Nvidia boss, the Times said. In a message to company employees released Sunday, the Nvidia chief acknowledged having an affair and apologized to his family and company staff. “I was unfaithful to my wife,” he said. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” Jensen Huang is a huge figure in the artificial intelligence revolution and a close informal adviser to US President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly spoken out against regulating the industry so as not to let China gain the upper hand in the AI race. The Times said Alice Huang’s relationship with the Nvidia chief could have given her insights into Trump’s thinking around AI. The issue of AI is likely to arise during Trump’s planned talks with President Xi Jinping later this month at a summit in China. Asked whether the Nvidia chief would be joining the president’s trip to Asia, which includes the Asia-Pacific summit in China’s Shenzhen on Sunday, Trump told reporters: “I don’t know but I’ll certainly take him.” Trump said Huang was “a fine person, but you never know what’s going on. I’m sure — I hope everything’s fine. He’s done such an incredible job.” – ‘Speculation’ – Nvidia said in a statement it had opened an independent probe “in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” The statement added: “While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information.” The Chinese government has dismissed the Times report as “groundless speculation.” China is in a race for tech dominance with the United States, which restricts the export to China of the most cutting-edge silicon chips. Nvidia, a global leader in producing chips used to train and run AI models, is one of the world’s most valuable companies. Megaspeed was under scrutiny for possibly steering Nvidia AI chips to China, the Times report said, citing unnamed sources briefed on the matter. Trump was briefed on the intelligence findings about Huang’s relationship with the businesswoman roughly a year ago and chose not to act on the information, the Times report said. item.title: Death Toll From Saudi Attack In Yemen Rises To 44
item.description: The death toll from Saudi strikes on Yemen’s Sanaa province climbed to 44, including more than 20 children, the Houthis said on their television channel Monday. A 2022 truce that had paused fighting in Yemen’s long-running conflict fell apart in July, restarting fighting between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government. Saudi Arabia has since traded blows with the Houthis, who have struck Saudi airports, energy infrastructure and military sites. “The toll from the Saudi enemy’s massacre in the Alshariyah area of Bani Hushaysh, east of Sanaa, has risen to 84 casualties: 44 martyrs and 40 wounded,” the Houthis’ ministry of health said, according to the group’s Almasirah TV channel. Yemenis carry a body recovered from the rubble of a destroyed building after an airstrike reportedly carried out by Saudi Arabia on a village in the Bani Hushaysh district, located on the eastern outskirts of Sanaa on November 7, 2026. It said 21 children and 10 women were among those killed. “Rescue teams are still searching for the missing,” it added. The fresh toll comes after the Houthis claimed on Sunday an attack on the financial district of the Saudi capital Riyadh, with eyewitnesses saying they saw damage to a skyscraper belonging to oil giant Aramco. The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed in the impoverished country. item.title: Trump vows comeback as bitter showdown with Congress looms
item.description: Donald Trump vowed a political comeback Sunday as the major parties clashed over Democrat threats to prosecute top administration officials after the president’s Republicans lost control of Congress in midterm elections. The devastating results in last Tuesday’s vote leave Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year ‘lame duck’ period of his White House tenure. It also opens the door to multiple investigations by the Democrat-controlled Congress of the president, his family and senior members of his administration. On political talk shows Sunday, incoming congressional leaders from the Democratic Party promised to hold Trump and his aides to account, while the president’s top law officer resolved to defend them and Trump dug in his heels on social media. “America took a giant step back in History with the results of the last Election,” Trump said in a post on Truth Social, adding that the stock market that had grown during his tenure took a loss after the vote. “But have no fear, we will be back, BIGGER AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE!” On Friday, a defiant Trump appointed hardline advisor Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff, signaling a bare-knuckle fightback — even though many Republicans, including Vice President JD Vance, have reflected on why they had lost so badly at the ballot box. Miller was architect of Trump’s tough immigration policy, which analysts have identified as a contributing factor to the unpopularity of Republicans and their election debacle. Amid Democrat threats for administration officials to “lawyer up,” Trump said Saturday he was ordering the Justice Department to examine Democratic threats to impeach members of his administration, likening it to “extortion.” – Impeaching Hegseth? – With control of committees in both chambers of Congress, Democrats can summon officials, demand documents and hold public hearings, putting Trump and his senior aides under intense scrutiny. Likely subjects include the Trump family’s business and cryptocurrency dealings, government contracts involving billionaire Elon Musk, cuts to federal agencies, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war. Hakeem Jeffries, set to become speaker of the new Democrat-controlled House of Representatives, said he would support an effort to oust Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, a key architect of the war on Iran that began in February. “I’m a hard yes on the Hegseth resolution,” Jeffries told ABC, when asked about a Republican lawmaker’s reported plan to introduce an impeachment motion as early as Monday. “The so-called secretary of defense has abused his power, undermined our national security and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has skyrocketed prices on the American people and made the country less safe. item.title: Iran War ‘Highly Unlikely’ To Resume, Says Trump
item.description: US President Donald Trump cast doubt on renewed fighting with Iran, telling CNN it was “highly unlikely,” ahead of a meeting with mediator Qatar’s prime minister on Monday. Trump has threatened to resume strikes in recent weeks, with US media reports suggesting that hostilities could restart after last Tuesday’s midterm elections. The president told CNN in an interview on Sunday that renewed fighting was “highly unlikely,” but warned that his decision “depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement.” “I would if necessary, but we hit them really hard. I hit them so hard. You don’t know how hard I hit them,” he said. Trump is scheduled to meet Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, who is also the country’s foreign minister, at the White House on Monday. The meeting will be Trump’s first with a foreign leader since a massive midterm loss that saw his Republican Party lose control of Congress. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi suggested on Sunday that peace talks had been paused while the political fallout of the vote was being assessed. “For the past few days, there has been no more travel (by mediators), and the reason for this is the shock that the election results in the United States have caused to everyone,” Araghchi told state television. “We now have to see how long it will take for them to digest these results, in order to determine how we are going to move forward,” he added. ‘They Had Enough’ Smoke rises following an Israeli controlled-explosion on the village of Kfartibnit as seen from Nabatieh in southern Lebanon on July 29, 2026.(Photo by Ammar Ammar / AFP) / | Ammar Ammar / AFP Trump has acknowledged that the highly unpopular war with Iran — which began with US-Israeli strikes in late February — was at least partially responsible for the Republicans’ defeat. Araghchi said Monday that the US president “clearly recognizes that the vast majority of Americans are disgusted with Israel.” “Americans are evidently sick and tired of Israel bamboozling US administrations into Forever Wars,” Araghchi said on X. “They had enough. So has our region.” In Sunday’s CNN interview, Trump once again suggested that the economic pressure Iran is under will force its leaders into accepting the United States’ terms. “They’re a failing nation. It just came out, you saw this year, 301 percent inflation,” Trump claimed. “They’re withering away financially. We’ve hit them militarily. We could finish them off.” Iran’s official figures put inflation at nearly 90 percent year-on-year in September. item.title: SON uploads MANCAP-certified products online to check fakes
item.description: The Standards Organisation of Nigeria, SON, has uploaded the list of products certified under its Mandatory Conformity Assessment Programme, MANCAP, to its official website to enable consumers to identify and patronise quality Nigerian-made products. Director-General of SON, Dr Ifeanyi Okeke, disclosed this at the CANEX WKND 2026 held at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly National Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos. Okeke, who was represented by the Director, Corporate Affairs Department, Mrs Talatu Ethan, said the initiative would enable consumers to verify certified products and make informed purchasing decisions. He said: “This development will help consumers find and buy quality products easily. It puts the power of choice in the hands of the Nigerian consumer, and it rewards manufacturers who have done the right thing by meeting our standards.” The SON boss urged members of the public to visit the organisation’s website to verify certified products, while encouraging them to report products bearing fake or questionable certification marks. He explained that SON’s participation at CANEX WKND 2026 was aimed at taking its quality assurance message directly to manufacturers, small business owners and consumers. “Our presence here is about meeting businesses where they are. Many creative and small enterprises have excellent products but do not know how to get them certified. Certification opens doors to bigger markets, here at home and across Africa, and it protects the consumer,” he said. At its exhibition stand, SON officials engaged exhibitors and visitors on product certification under the Nigerian Industrial Standards, NIS. They also educated participants on MANCAP, which covers locally manufactured products, and the SON Conformity Assessment Programme, SONCAP, applicable to imported products. Visitors were also sensitised on how to identify substandard and counterfeit products, verify the SON authentication mark and report suspicious goods. Small and medium-sized enterprises, SMEs, received guidance on the certification process, including application, product testing and eventual approval. Okeke stressed that locally manufactured products must meet international standards to compete effectively in global markets, particularly under the Federal Government’s Nigeria First policy. item.title: Nigerian woman entrepreneur wins award at World Investment Forum
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole A Nigerian woman entrepreneur, Biobele Oyibo, has won the Technology Award at the 2026 Empretec Women in Business Awards held during the 9th World Investment Forum in Doha, Qatar. Oyibo, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Earlybean, was recognised for leveraging technology to promote financial literacy and inclusion among young people. The awards organised under the theme, “Women-led businesses and the art of scale”, celebrated women entrepreneurs driving innovation, sustainability and business growth across four categories: Leadership, Sustainability, Innovation and Technology. The event brought together entrepreneurs, investors, policymakers and business leaders to celebrate the winners and connect them with funding, markets, expertise and networks to expand their businesses. The awards highlighted the role of women-led enterprises in creating jobs, deploying new technologies and addressing economic, social and environmental challenges. Other winners included Sandra Letio of Uganda, who received the Leadership Award for building an agribusiness that works with more than 5,000 smallholder farmers; and Paula Gianserra of Argentina, winner of the Sustainability Award for advancing forest restoration through artificial intelligence, biotechnology and drone seeding. The Innovation Award went to Aisha Albinali of Qatar, Co-Founder of Wafir, for transforming traditional savings practices into a financial technology solution, and Adriana Fernandes of Brazil, Chief Executive Officer of Mátrika Special Foods, for improving access to safe, quality food for people with allergies and dietary restrictions. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 9, 2026
item.description: The dollar-to-naira exchange rate remains a key indicator for businesses, importers and Nigerians monitoring developments in the foreign exchange market. The Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) serves as the official platform for foreign currency transactions, while the parallel market remains an alternative source of dollars for individuals and businesses. As of Monday morning, November 9, 2026, the latest available official NFEM closing rate stood at approximately ₦1,346.79 per dollar, based on the November 6 market data published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) In the parallel market, the dollar was quoted at approximately ₦1,415 to ₦1,430, depending on the dealer and location. This puts the gap between the official and parallel markets at about ₦68 to ₦83 per dollar. The parallel-market figures are indicative and may change throughout the day depending on dollar supply and demand. item.title: Flamingos Arrive In Abuja After FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup Victory
item.description: Victorious Flamingos landed in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on Monday morning after their win at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup on Saturday. The team won their first FIFA Under-17 Women’s World Cup title after defeating Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final, with goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku securing the historic victory. The Flamingos became the first African team to win the competition, with goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku securing the historic victory. Officials of the Nigeria Football Federation and some supporters received the victorious Flamingos, who landed in the early hours of the day, at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport in Abuja. The triumph is another landmark for a team that had already established itself as one of Africa’s leading sides at the age-grade level. Before travelling to Morocco, the Flamingos won the 2026 WAFU-B U-17 Girls Cup in Côte d’Ivoire, recording five victories from five matches, scoring 17 goals and conceding just once. ‘Victory Not A Fluke’ Flamingos head coach Hakeem Busari has praised his players for their resilience and tactical discipline after their impressive campaign at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, while expressing optimism about African football’s future. Busari, in a post-match interview, said the performance of African teams at the tournament reflected growing quality, character and competitiveness, despite the challenges posed by strong opposition. The Flamingos became the first African team to win the competition, with goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku securing the historic victory. He noted that the Flamingos had competed in a difficult group that included the defending champions, adding that the experience demonstrated the progress being made in African women’s youth football. “What we are seeing now is not a fluke. It is about development, it is about character, and it is about fighting from the beginning to really get it right. So we are elated and happy,” he said. The coach also expressed hope that more African teams would progress beyond the knockout stages in future editions of the competition and eventually reach the final. Reflecting on the Flamingos’ encounter with Japan, Busari explained that his technical crew had identified the Japanese team’s strength in winning second balls and exploiting spaces behind defensive lines. He said the team adjusted its approach to limit Japan’s attacking opportunities, particularly by directing long balls into spaces rather than areas where the opposition could easily gain possession. Busari explained that the Flamingos initially sought to score early before adopting a more cautious approach after taking the lead, but Japan eventually found an equaliser through a set-piece situation. He described the encounter as a tactical contest that required collective defending, discipline and effective game management. item.title: Manufacturers charged to deploy AI, energy-efficient technologies to cut costs
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN) has urged manufacturers to embrace Artificial Intelligence (AI), advanced technologies and energy-efficient solutions to tackle rising production costs, strengthen energy security and improve industrial competitiveness. The call was made at the 2026 Manufacturers Energy Security and Energy Efficiency Summit in Lagos, where industry leaders and government representatives examined the role of technology, sustainable energy supply and structured financing in addressing the energy challenges confronting Nigerian manufacturers. The event was jointly organised by Manufacturers Power Development Company Ltd. (MPDCL), GIZ and the Nigerian Energy Support Programme (NESP). President of MAN, Ifeanyi Okoye, said the industrial energy cost reduction and adoption programme would promote factory rooftop solar installations, battery energy storage systems, captive natural gas solutions, and smart energy management networks. He said the programme was aimed at addressing the rising cost of energy, which had significantly affected manufacturing operations and competitiveness. According to him, manufacturers spend about 40 per cent of their profits addressing energy challenges, while high electricity tariffs, unreliable grid supply, and dependence on fossil fuels continued to undermine industrial production. “The summit is to facilitate access to long-term financing instruments, climate funds, green investments, and asset-financing mechanisms to support manufacturers’ transition to more efficient energy systems,” he said. In his comment, Director-General of MAN, Segun Ajayi-Kadir, said the adoption of emerging technologies had become critical to improving production efficiency, reducing energy consumption and strengthening the resilience of manufacturing operations. He noted that AI and smart manufacturing systems could help industries optimise energy use, minimise production losses, lower operating costs and improve product quality, particularly amid persistent electricity supply challenges. Chairman, Board of Directors, MPDCL, John Aluya, noted that the high cost of self-generation had reduced manufacturers’ profit margins and weakened their competitiveness. He stressed that reliable and affordable energy was critical to the survival of Nigerian industries, adding that the summit was meant to explore practical solutions, including solar photovoltaic systems, battery energy storage, captive gas power, energy efficiency, and carbon credit monetisation. In his keynote address, Ulf Brackmann, Chief Executive Officer of IKAPITAL Family Office & Friends, said AI could significantly boost industrial productivity and create new employment opportunities rather than displace workers, urging manufacturers to take advantage of the opportunities offered by technological innovation. item.title: Power outages, rising costs slow manufacturing growth —NESG
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole Frequent power outages, rising production costs and limited access to credit are slowing manufacturing growth in Nigeria, with businesses struggling to sustain operations amid persistent infrastructure challenges, the October 2026 Business Confidence Monitor (BCM) by the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG) has shown. The report indicated that manufacturing remained in expansion territory in October, but its Current Business Performance Index declined to 107.3 points from 108.4 points in September and 111.3 points in October 2025, reflecting a moderation in business activity. It identified incessant power outages, inadequate raw material supplies, high rental costs, limited access to credit and infrastructure deficiencies as major constraints confronting manufacturers during the month. According to NESG, these challenges continued to amplify operating costs, despite sustained expansion in business activities across the economy. The impact was particularly evident in key manufacturing subsectors. Textile, Apparel and Footwear slipped into contraction territory, with its performance index plunging to 99.7 points in October from 127.5 points in September. Cement also remained in contraction at 94.5 points, while Food, Beverage and Tobacco was the only one of the three major manufacturing subsectors to record improved performance and remain in expansion territory. The report’s findings underscore the growing burden of unreliable electricity on manufacturers, who depend on stable power supply to sustain production lines, process raw materials and maintain factory operations. Frequent outages force businesses to rely on alternative energy sources, adding to production costs and weakening their competitiveness. At the broader economy level, Nigeria’s Current Business Performance Index moderated to 115.4 points in October from 117.8 points in September, although it remained above the 111.3 points recorded in October 2025. All sectors remained in expansion territory, but only Trade and Services recorded improved performance compared with the preceding month. Agriculture, Manufacturing and Non-Manufacturing experienced slower growth. The cost pressures were also reflected in the NESG’s business indicators. The cost of doing business sub-index stood at 45.2 points in October, while the prices sub-index was 65.5 points, both significantly below the 100-point neutral threshold, indicating that most firms continued to face elevated operating costs and producer prices. Despite the challenges, the Future Business Expectations Index rose to 130.8 points in October from 128.9 points in September, signalling improved optimism about business conditions over the next one to three months. Manufacturing recorded an expectations index of 145.1 points, behind Trade at 194 points, but ahead of Non-Manufacturing at 135 points. item.title: ACAMB advises bank customers against phishing scams
item.description: The Association of Corporate Communication and Marketing Professionals in Banks (ACAMB) has urged bank customers to remain vigilant against phishing scams and other forms of cyber fraud, warning that criminals are increasingly using fake bank alerts, cloned websites and impersonation accounts to steal sensitive financial information. The warning follows a fraudulent text message impersonating various banks. FactCheckAfrica debunked the message, finding that the link it contained led to a cloned internet banking website designed to steal customers’ login credentials, BVNs, card details and transaction PINs. The incident highlights the risks associated with digital banking fraud in Nigeria. In June, Wema Bank suspended its engagements on X, (formerly known as Twitter) amid reports of more than 70 fake accounts impersonating the bank and its ALAT platform. In August, Zenith Bank Plc disclosed that it was investigating unauthorised access to customer data linked to a global cyberattack. ACAMB President, Jide Sipe, warned that fraudsters were increasingly adopting sophisticated methods to impersonate trusted banking brands and steal customers’ personal information, making their schemes difficult to distinguish from legitimate communications. “When a scam message carries your name, your phone number or your bank’s logo, it looks real. That is exactly why customers must slow down. No bank in Nigeria will ask you to confirm your PIN, password, OTP or BVN through a link,” Sipe said. Sipe acknowledged the efforts of banks to strengthen fraud detection and customer protection, alongside regulatory measures introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria’s mandatory cybersecurity self assessment guide. He stressed, however, that these efforts must be complemented by customer awareness and vigilance, particularly when handling requests for sensitive banking information. “Banks can strengthen their security systems, but fraudsters continue to find ways to exploit unsuspecting customers. We must all remain vigilant. Always pause, verify requests through official channels and report anything suspicious before taking action,” he added. Sipe urged customers to avoid clicking links in unsolicited messages asking them to verify, reactivate or secure their bank accounts. He also warned against sharing personal identification numbers (PINs), passwords, one-time passwords (OTPs), card verification values (CVVs) or BVNs in response to suspicious requests. Customers should verify such requests directly with their banks through official mobile applications, verified social media accounts or published customer service numbers. item.title: World Ports Confab: FG woos global investors with maritime reforms
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) has intensified efforts to attract global investment into Nigeria’s maritime sector by showcasing the Federal Government’s ongoing port reforms and investor-friendly policies at the World Ports Conference, highlighting opportunities for private sector participation, improved port efficiency and sustainable growth. Speaking at the ongoing World Ports Conference in London, Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority, Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, showcased President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s maritime policies and its positioning of Nigeria’s Ports as Africa’s biggest economy that is yearning for global investment. He affirmed that the speed of growth and development in the country’s ports signifies the huge opportunities investors should tap into, adding that the current administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has put policies in place that are investment friendly. The NPA boss identified Nigeria’s huge population, urbanization, and infrastructural gaps in the ports as attractive opportunities for investment in its maritime and associated sectors. Dantsoho, who is also the Vice- President of the International Association of Ports & Harbours (IAPH) and doubles as Chairman of the Port Management Association of West and Central Africa (PMAWCA) told investors that Africa’s untapped resources remain the best destination for ports investment and development. He said the government alone cannot fund development of bigger or deeper sea ports and other similar projects hence the need for investors to take advantage of such opportunities across the continent. Dantsoho affirmed that “Nigeria has the highest population in Africa. So, the speed of growth is something that really should concern us. For example, in Nigeria, only recently, about 3 years ago, we commissioned the first deep sea port in Nigeria, which is called Lekki Deep Sea Port, that was funded by the Chinese government in relationship with China Harbor, and the expenditure cost us $1.6 billion to build Lekki in Lagos. item.title: BoI advocates investment in industrial clusters to boost Lagos economy
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe The Bank of Industry (BOI) has called for increased investment in industrial clusters, reliable power supply and supporting infrastructure to boost productivity, attract private capital and strengthen the Lagos State economy. Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, BoI, Dr. Olasupo Olusi made this call in a keynote address delivered at the 4th edition of the Lagos Economic Outlook 2027 Discourse, themed, ‘“Development Pathways, Emerging Risks and Strategic Policy Priorities.’ Represented by Dr. Isa Omagu, General Manager, MD/CEO’s Office, BoI, Olusi said investment in industrial clusters, particularly along major industrial and port corridors, would help businesses overcome production constraints, reduce operating costs and improve their competitiveness. He also said Lagos must assess economic progress by the improvements businesses and residents experience, rather than relying solely on economic growth figures and public spending. “The test is whether Lagos becomes more productive and more liveable,” he said. He identified electricity costs, traffic congestion, access to appropriate financing and institutional coordination as major constraints to business productivity. “A manufacturer needs reliable electricity. A worker needs a commute that does not consume productive hours. Firms need predictable approvals, appropriate finance and customers,” he said. Olusi urged the state to prioritise investment in power infrastructure serving industrial clusters, faster freight movement, streamlined business approvals, flood-resilient commercial routes and skills development. Speaking at the event, Lagos State Commissioner for Economic Planning and Budget, Mr. Ope George, said the ministry would continue to coordinate economic intelligence, development planning, budget management and performance monitoring in support of Lagos State’s long-term development aspirations. He said the 2027 economic outlook provided an opportunity to consolidate the state’s achievements, address structural challenges and strengthen its position as a competitive and resilient economy. “Our focus goes beyond economic projections. It is about shaping policies that will strengthen competitiveness, promote inclusive growth and secure a sustainable future for Lagos State,” George said. Earlier, Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Economic Planning and Budget, Mrs. Olayinka Ojo, highlighted the state’s development planning, budget monitoring and performance evaluation frameworks. She said Lagos was strengthening evidence-based governance through its long-term development plan, Medium-Term Expenditure Framework, annual budgets and regular monitoring of revenue, expenditure and project delivery. Ojo also highlighted the government’s engagement with communities and the use of platforms to improve citizens’ access to information on public projects and social intervention programmes. item.title: Customs frees 98 containers of power equipment stranded for 20 years
item.description: •Cargoes to ease pressure on substations, strengthen national grid — Tegbe By Udeme Akpan The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has released 98 containers of electricity transmission equipment stranded at the nation’s ports, some for up to 20 years, in a move expected to strengthen the national grid and improve electricity supply across the country. The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, disclosed this in Lagos, stating that 44 containers were released from ENL Terminal, while another 54 were cleared from APMT and Sun & Moon Terminals. He said the 98 containers represented part of more than 300 containers of transmission equipment held at the ports. The equipment, comprising high-capacity transformers, cables and switchgear, was procured to expand the transmission network, address overloaded substations and improve electricity delivery nationwide. Tegbe said: “The equipment was procured to expand the transmission network and relieve overloaded substations. Its detention stalled projects, kept existing substations under heavy strain, exposed valuable assets to deterioration and accumulated charges on the cargoes.” He noted that the prolonged detention of the equipment had imposed additional costs on businesses, households and public institutions, which continued to grapple with unreliable electricity supply. Also speaking, the Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adeniyi, said the Service had commenced processes to clear the containers in collaboration with the Ministry of Power, the Nigerian Ports Authority and terminal operators. He said: “The release follows the President’s directive for immediate clearance and for agencies to resolve outstanding charges and administrative bottlenecks without delay.” Adeniyi pledged to work with the Minister until all the containers were cleared, while appealing to terminal operators to support the national effort. The Minister disclosed that an inspection of the recovered equipment showed that most of the items remained useful and viable. He said: “When evacuated, it will be verified, tested and refurbished where necessary, then deployed to project sites to complete stalled installations, relieve overloaded substations and strengthen constrained transmission corridors.” The post Customs frees 98 containers of power equipment stranded for 20 years appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: COP31 Opens As Climate, Geopolitical Pressures Mount
item.description: The UN’s annual climate talks kick off Monday in Turkey as rising temperatures heighten the urgency of action, with financial constraints and geopolitical tensions complicating efforts to secure global cooperation. More than 100,000 people are expected to attend COP31 in a sprawling expo centre in the Mediterranean seaside city of Antalya over the next two weeks. Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are facing tough discussions over how to accelerate the energy transition and provide funds to help developing nations cope with the worsening climate emergency. But observers say few major breakthroughs are expected as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the US war with Iran and Russia’s conflict in Ukraine. The climate emergency, meanwhile, continued to wreak havoc this year as punishing heatwaves baked Europe, wildfires raged in Indonesia, and a glacier collapse triggered devastating floods in Nepal. An exceptionally strong El Niño climate phenomenon is forecast to peak later this year, adding to extreme weather and possibly helping to make 2026 or 2027 the hottest year on record. The outlook is bleak: the United Nations warned in September that global temperatures were on course to exceed 1.5C above preindustrial levels, breaching the most ambitious threshold set by the Paris Agreement. “Global leaders must pull us back from the brink and commit to rapidly transitioning away from fossil fuels and expanding renewable energy, an imperative reinforced by the current energy affordability crisis,” said Rachel Cleetus, climate programme director at the Union of Concerned Scientists. A woman walks inside the COP31 venue at the Antalya Expo Center on November 8, 2026, ahead of the opening of the UN climate conference. ‘Clean’ Electrification? Turkey is presiding over COP31, with Australia leading negotiations under an unusual arrangement that settled a dispute over who would host the conference. The partners have branded the summit as the “implementation COP”, focusing on turning commitments into concrete action after years of pledges and ambitious announcements. Turkey is promoting an “action agenda” alongside the formal negotiations that encourages countries to support non-binding pledges on issues from artificial intelligence to waste management. Its centrepiece is an “electrification” drive to raise the share of global energy demand met by electricity from around 20 percent today to 35 percent by 2035. But the initiative could become a source of friction. The European Union has called for “clean” electrification, a term that could spark debate over the role of fossil fuels in the Turkish proposal. Countries committed to transition away from fossil fuels in a landmark pact at COP28 in Dubai in 2023 but have struggled to agree on how to turn that pledge into action. item.title: 2026 Lagos Trade Fair: We’re poised to turn stability into prosperity — Tinubu
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole President Bola Tinubu has said Nigeria’s next economic priority is to translate the gains of ongoing reforms into prosperity through enterprise, industrial growth and expanded trade. Tinubu spoke at the weekend, at the opening of the 40th Lagos International Trade Fair, organised by the Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI), at Tafawa Balewa Square, Lagos. The president, represented by the Minister of State for Industry, Senator John Enoh, said the Federal Government had made significant progress in stabilising the economy, adding that the focus must now shift to stimulating production, creating jobs and expanding business opportunities. “The emergency is over. The foundation has been repaired. Our task now is to turn stability into prosperity, and enterprise is at the heart of that task,” he said. Highlighting the administration’s economic achievements, Tinubu said Nigeria’s gross external reserves rose to approximately $55.07 billion in October 2026, the highest level in 18 years, while net reserves exceeded $40 billion, from less than $4 billion in 2023. He also noted that inflation declined to 14.63 per cent in September 2026, while the economy grew by 4.43 per cent in the second quarter, describing the figures as evidence of improving economic fundamentals. On trade, the President said non-oil exports exceeded $6.1 billion in 2025, while capital importation reached about $21 billion, expressing optimism that Nigerian businesses could leverage the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) to access wider markets. He, however, stressed that sustainable economic growth must be driven by domestic production and value addition rather than dependence on imports. Tinubu said the National Industrial Policy provides a roadmap for strengthening manufacturing, deepening local value chains and converting Nigeria’s raw materials into finished products. He disclosed that the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment and its agencies supported more than 115,000 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in 2025, promising continued efforts to improve their access to finance, electricity and markets. He described industrial and trade policies as complementary, stressing that while industry provides goods for export, trade creates markets for locally manufactured products. The President also welcomed exhibitors from more than 20 countries and said Nigeria would host the Intra-African Trade Fair for the first time in 2027, in partnership with Afreximbank. item.title: Comedian Russell Brand To Be Sentenced For Rape, Assaults
item.description: British comedian and TV star Russell Brand, who became a household name in the 2000s as a sex-obsessed provocateur, will find out on Monday how long he will spend in jail, after he was convicted of rape and sexual assaults. Brand’s conviction last week marked the final blow in a scandal-hit showbiz career that saw him embody the anything-goes culture of 2000s British TV and radio. On Monday, he will be sentenced at London’s Southwark Crown Court, where he was told by the judge he faced a “significant custodial term” after being found guilty of one rape and three sexual assaults against four women, committed between 2004 and 2009. The maximum sentence in the UK for rape is life imprisonment. Brand, 51, who was cleared of two other alleged rapes and one count of attempted indecent assault, was remanded in custody and spent the weekend in a cell. He is facing further investigations after London’s Metropolitan Police said it was probing rape allegations by two more women. (FILES) British actor and comedian Russell Brand addresses an anti-austerity rally in Parliament Square in London on June 21, 2014. London’s Metropolitan Police on Friday said it had charged comedian and actor Russell Brand with rape and a number of other sexual offences. (Photo by Justin TALLIS / AFP) From Channel 4 to MTV and an eponymous primetime show on BBC Radio 2, the wild-haired comedian passed through major British media houses in the 2000s, where his obsession with sex contributed to his notoriety. That behaviour was also a feature of the high-profile trial, with Brand admitting that he had been “extremely promiscuous” and had used his fame to “facilitate sexual access”, although he denied the charges. He was accompanied to court most days by his wife Laura Gallacher, with whom he has three children. Calling him a “wonderful father to our children”, Gallacher told the jury that when they first dated in 2006: “It was clear it was difficult for him to be monogamous.” She said she was “very aware” of Brand’s promiscuity, as “you could read about it regularly in the papers”. British comedian and actor Russell Brand (C) leaves following a hearing at Southwark Crown Court in south London on May 30, 2025. Brand pleaded not guilty to five charges of rape and sexual assault. (Photo by HENRY NICHOLLS / AFP) ‘Shapeshifter’ Brand’s hypersexualised persona was a running joke in tabloids, with the comedian named “shagger of the year” three years in a row by The Sun newspaper from 2006-2009. “He’s a bit of a shapeshifter,” then-showbiz editor of The Sun, Gordon Smart told Channel 4. “He would present to you as he thought appropriate, quite chameleon-like.” Born to working-class parents in Essex, east of London in 1975, Brand dropped out of drama school before joining MTV at the age of 25. He was fired for turning up to work dressed as Osama bin Laden following the 9/11 terror attacks and for inviting his drug dealer into the studios. item.title: The mounting debt burden should terrify Nigerians, by Dele Sobowale
item.description: •Tinubu seeks $20.5bn; €1.04bn foreign loans to fund projects – Vanguard, October 28, 2026 •Debt worse than leprosy, Obasanjo replies Tinubu — Report, October 31, 2026 Seldom do I find myself on the same side with former President Obasanjo on matters concerning national affairs. Right now, I am on all fours with Baba Iyabo with regard to his position on President Tinubu’s request for fresh loans amounting to over $21 billion or N29.4 trillion. The debt burden is now approximately N160 trillion. Given a shamelessly rubber stamp Senate, it is a foregone conclusion that it will be approved. By December, the total debt would total N189.4 trillion. It was about N100 trillion when Buhari left the nation’s “economy on the brink of bankruptcy” – according to Tinubu. Read Also: Economy: Food warehouses now split wholesale bags as retailers battle inflation Putting the request into historical perspective would help to understand the loan request better. From 1978, under General Obasanjo, when the first $2.8 billion loan was taken, it took the country 21 years until 1999 to accumulate $36 billion or N50.4 trillion at current exchange rates. Minister of Finance, Dr Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala got us out of the debt trap in 2004. By the time President Jonathan left office in 2015, the debt had risen to $30 billion or N42 trillion once again. Eight years of Buhari’s financial mismanagement racked up N58 trillion. By the time this fresh loan is approved and taken, Tinubu would have added N89.4 trillion in just three and a half years; and, this might not be the last loan request before May 29, 2027. Whoever is President next year might be facing a debt burden well over N200 trillion. When last year I wrote that borrowing is the opium of the governing classes, it never occurred to me that the addiction could be as bad as this. Obasanjo is absolutely correct; mindless borrowing, tainted with corrupt and concealed self-interest, is indeed worse than leprosy. Lepers sometimes have children without leprosy. The malady is invariably restricted to one person and one generation. Nigeria’s debt load, made infinitely worse by Tinubu’s fiscal policy mismanagement, is already visiting diseases more virulent than leprosy on millions of Nigerians alive; and will savage millions more for at least three generations for one inescapable reason – inability to repay from revenue generation. item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The Presidential Candidate of Allied Peoples Movement, APM, Engr. Seyi Makinde, declared weekend he had no political godfather other than God, expressing confidence that divine backing and the support of Nigerians would propel him to victory in the 2027 presidential election. Makinde recalled how he defied the absence of political godfathers to become governor of Oyo State in 2019, expressing confidence that his presidential ambition would also be sustained by faith and popular support. “When I said in Oyo State in 2018 that I would like to be governor, somebody asked me, ‘Governor of which Rotary District?’ I said governor of Oyo State, and they asked, ‘with no godfather; nobody in politics who can stand in for you?’ I responded by saying, well, I have God the Father. He said the documents provided clear direction for his administration and helped ensured that promises made to the people were translated into concrete actions. Makinde said he had adopted a similar approach in preparing for the presidency, with the RESET NIGERIA agenda built around four pillars: security, the economy, education and the socio-political space. Presenting the manifesto, he challenged Nigerians to hold him accountable for the commitments contained in the document. “I want Nigerians to be able to hold me accountable, not just through promises but through documented commitments. item.title: ADC to APC: Test your popularity at polls, stop using courts to block us
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA—African Democratic Congress, ADC, has dared the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, to test its popularity at the ballot box, rather than resort to court processes to frustrate the opposition party’s participation in the 2027 general election. Read Also: What is 25% requirement in Nigeria’s presidential election? The challenge came from the Director-General of ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Austin Akobundu, who said the massive reception accorded the party’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, in Sokoto State, and his running mate, Rotimi Amaechi, in Kebbi State, reflected growing public enthusiasm for the party and the desire for an alternative political direction. In a statement yesterday, Akobundu, while thanking supporters and residents who turned out to welcome the candidates, accused the federal government and APC-led administration of attempting to shut the ADC out of the political contest through what he described as a backdoor judicial process. “If the federal government and the APC believe they have the capacity to win, let them allow a free and fair election. Let Nigerians choose without intimidation, obstruction or interference. “They must stop trying to muzzle the political space, using a backdoor court process to remove us from the contest,’’ he said. On the need to protect democratic competition, Akobundu insisted that Nigerians must be free to listen to competing political ideas, attend rallies and choose their leaders without interference. “The ballot must remain the people’s choice, and every party must be allowed to campaign freely,” he said. While urging party supporters not to be distracted by the political tensions, the ADC campaign chief called for restraint and sustained grassroots mobilisation. “Let us continue to campaign peacefully and confidently, knowing that the people’s will must prevail,” he pleaded. Akobundu said ADC would continue to take its message of affordable living, opportunity and national renewal to Nigerians across the country, while expressing appreciation to those who welcomed its candidates in Sokoto and Kebbi states. item.title: Nigeria must tackle insecurity, unemployment — Obasanjo
item.description: Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has called for urgent action to address worsening insecurity, unemployment and poverty in Nigeria. Read Also: How presidential elections are won in Nigeria He also warned that leadership failures were forcing citizens to seek better opportunities abroad, often through dangerous migration routes. Obasanjo, who spoke during a panel session, themed “Lest We Forget” at the Creative Africa Nexus Weekend 2026, organised by the African Export-Import Bank in Lagos State weekend, reflected on Nigeria’s security situation since independence and said the country must confront the governance failures responsible for declining safety and economic opportunities. “We just have to do what we should do to provide job opportunities, to stem the tide of impunity, to stem the tide of poverty, to stem the tide of kidnapping and insecurity,” he said. Obasanjo recalled returning to Nigeria in 1959 after completing his military training in Britain, noting that he could travel freely across the country without fear of attacks or kidnapping. “I came back to this country after my commission as an officer in Britain in 1959. And I could go anywhere; I was posted to the north; I could go anywhere in the north, by myself alone, by day, by night,” he said. Contrasting that experience with the current security situation, he questioned how Nigeria had deteriorated to the point where citizens could no longer travel safely across several parts of the country. “Now, if you can’t do that, what has gone wrong? We have to correct what has gone wrong,” he stated. He argued that unemployment, particularly among university graduates, had become a major source of economic desperation, making it difficult to discourage young Africans from leaving their countries in search of opportunities. According to him, governments cannot continue producing graduates without creating sufficient employment opportunities and expect them to remain economically productive. Obasanjo recalled an encounter with Nigerians arrested for drug-related offences, explaining that one of the suspects had attributed his involvement in the illegal trade to the loss of legitimate employment. He said the encounter demonstrated how economic hardship could push otherwise productive individuals towards desperate decisions, although he stopped short of justifying criminal activities. Addressing irregular migration, Obasanjo said he had interacted with Africans who attempted to reach Europe through the Sahara Desert and the Mediterranean Sea, describing their experiences as distressing. “I have got those people who have attempted to cross, and the story they told me is pathetic. Some die in the Sahara, some die in the Mediterranean,” he said. item.title: Economy: Food warehouses now split wholesale bags as retailers battle inflation
item.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan A quiet transformation is reshaping how branded food items and cooking oils move from distribution warehouses to neighborhood shops, across major wholesale food markets in Nigeria. Read Also: Can 142m Nigerian youths change 2027 elections narrative? Faced with persistent inflation, tight liquidity, and shrinking consumer purchasing power, Economy&Lifestyle findings show that bulk food warehouses are increasingly breaking down standard 50-kilogram sacks and full cartons into half-measures for small-scale retailers. Traditionally, wholesale depots in major distribution centers across the country operated on strict minimum-order volumes. Retailers were required to purchase full 50kg bags of rice, beans, or garri, full cartons of noodles, or 25-liter kegs of vegetable oil. However, as wholesale prices are consistently rising over the past two years, many corner-shop owners and market stall traders are finding it difficult to raise the capital needed to restock full units across multiple product lines. In response, warehouse operators and major distributors have adapted their inventory models, introducing official ‘half-bag’ and ‘split-carton’ wholesale tiers. Instead of turning away undercapitalised buyers, depot managers now employ dedicated staff to weigh, re-bag, and seal 25kg portions of grains and split bulk cartons of packaged foods at wholesale rates. Alhaji Musa Danjuma, a bulk grain distributor, said: “If we insist on selling only full bags, our goods will sit in the warehouse until they spoil or expire. “A retailer, who used to buy 10 full bags of local parboiled rice can barely afford three today. “By splitting bags into halves and quarters at wholesale margins, we keep our stock moving and help small traders keep their shelves stocked.” The shift has provided immediate relief for micro-retailers who form the backbone of Nigeria’s informal food distribution network. For traders operating on thin daily margins, tying up scarce capital in a single full sack of beans or sugar often meant leaving customers without other essentials like pasta, seasoning cubes, or vegetable oil. “Before now, buying one full bag of brown beans took almost all my weekly capital,” said Mrs. Ngozi Okafor, a provision store owner. “Now, the warehouse allows me to pick half a bag of beans, half a bag of rice, and half a carton of spaghetti. “My shop looks full again, and my customers do not have to walk away empty-handed because I ran out of one items.” Market analysts note that while this fractional wholesale model keeps supply chains active, it introduces minor operational costs for warehouses, including extra packaging materials, labor for re-weighing, and heightened vigilance against weight discrepancies. To maintain trust, several wholesale associations have introduced standardised digital scales at loading bays so retailers can verify weights before payment. item.title: Election fever, Dangote Refinery to drive stock investors’ fortune at year end
item.description: By Peter Egwuatu The Nigerian stock market is projected to cross the N200 trillion market capitalisation by December 2026, while investors’ returns could exceed 57 per cent. Capital market analysts, who made the projections, said the anticipated listing of shares of Dangote Petroleum Refinery on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX), coupled with improved investor confidence, strong corporate earnings, increased market liquidity and favourable macroeconomic developments, would provide further impetus for the equities market. They also projected that the NGX All-Share Index (ASI), the market’s major performance indicator, could close the year at about 280,000 points. However, some analysts have warned that profit-taking, election-related uncertainties and global economic developments could trigger intermittent volatility. But the analysts agreed that the concern over 2027 general election is around possible policy change adding that if there are no major adverse economic policy developments capable of undermining investor confidence the impact of the election would be less severe. Market performance so far A review of the market’s performance Year-to-Date, YtD, as at last week, showed that investors’ wealth had increased by N62.76 trillion, representing a 60.47 per cent appreciation. Market capitalisation, which measures the total value of listed equities, rose from N99.376 trillion at the beginning of the year to N162.134 trillion last week. Similarly, the NGX ASI appreciated by 60.5 per cent, rising from 155,613.03 points at the beginning of the year to 249,710.59 points. The impressive performance has been supported by relative stability in the foreign exchange market, renewed investor confidence, strong corporate earnings, easing inflation, improved liquidity in the financial system and the decision of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to reduce the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) to 23 per cent. Analysts’ projections Speaking to Financial Vanguard on his projection for the year-end, Olatunde Amolegbe, immediate past President, Chartered Institute of Stockbrokers (CIS), and Managing Director, Arthur Stevens Asset Management Limited, said he remained cautiously optimistic about the equities market. He stated: “I remain cautiously optimistic about the Nigerian stock market for the rest of the year. My expectation is that the All-Share Index will deliver a full-year return of approximately 57.65%. “Although the market has recorded impressive gains so far, I expect some moderation in the coming weeks, as investors may take profits following the significant rally we have witnessed. We could also see some volatility as investors reposition their portfolios ahead of the new year. “On the positive side, relatively strong corporate earnings, improved investor confidence, increased domestic participation and ongoing economic reforms should continue to provide support for the market. item.title: Bandits burn 12 family members
item.description: Twelve members of the same family have been killed after armed bandits set their residence ablaze during an attack on Gidan Taba village in Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara State. Seven other residents were also abducted during the attack, which occurred on Saturday night in Dosara Birnin Kaya Ward, despite efforts by the community to alert security agencies. This is coming barely one week after bandits ambushed security personnel at Gidan Kano along the Gusau-Sokoto highway within the same local government and killed five policemen. A resident, who spoke to Daily Trust on condition of anonymity, said the attackers invaded the residence of one Mallam Muhammadu Sani at about 10 pm. 1 killed in NDC rally as attacks rise Middle Belt leaders’ visit to Tinubu raises unity questions He said 13 members of the family were trapped inside a room after locking themselves in to escape being abducted by the attackers. According to him, those inside the room included Sani, his two wives and their six children, as well as the wife of his younger brother and their three children. He said the bandits ordered the occupants to open the door, but when they refused, the attackers set the room ablaze. Only the wife of Sani’s younger brother reportedly escaped, while the remaining 12 occupants died from the intense heat and fire. The resident said the community immediately contacted the Maradun Local Government Chairman, Sanusi Ahmed Dosara, who made efforts to reach security formations for assistance. However, he said the security agencies could not intervene before the tragedy occurred. “We informed the local government chairman, Dosara, and he tried all he could to reach the security personnel. He told us he had spoken with different security formations, but nobody came to our rescue,” he said. He expressed disappointment that no security personnel responded to their distress calls despite the village’s proximity to Maradun town, where military and police formations are located. “Imagine, the distance between our village and Dosara is just about half a kilometre, while from Dosara to Maradun is about one kilometre. In total, it is just about one and a half kilometres between our village and the local government headquarters. “There is a military base in Maradun, a mobile police base and a police headquarters, yet none of them came to our aid until the bandits burnt the 12 people alive,” he said. Another resident confirmed that seven other people were abducted during the attack and remained in the custody of the bandits as of the time he spoke to Daily Trust. He appealed to security agencies to strengthen their presence in the area and take urgent measures to protect residents against further attacks. item.title: 2027 Elections: Lagos APC Candidate Hamzat Promises 4,000 CNG Buses, 77 Electric Ferries
item.description: The Lagos State governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Obafemi Hamzat, has promised to deploy 4,000 compressed natural gas (CNG) buses to move one million passengers daily as part of plans to ease transportation challenges in the state. Hamzat, the incumbent Deputy Governor, also disclosed plans to expand water transportation with 77 electric ferries and improve connectivity between different parts of Lagos through an integrated transport system. ﻿ He made the promises on Sunday during the Lagos governorship debate organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, comprising Channels Television, TVC News, Punch Newspaper, The Cable, and Vanguard Newspaper. Explaining his transportation plans, Hamzat said the objective was to reduce commuting time and give residents more opportunities to rest and spend time with their families. “The plan is to give back time to the citizens to plan, to rest, to spend with their family. There’s nowhere in Africa that the private sector has funded a rail. “Since BRT started, it has done 77 million journeys; that is with 1,000 buses. My plan says we will push it to 4,000 buses; the idea is to move one million people a day with 4,000 CNG buses, meaning up to 5,000, create BRt lane from Marina to Epe, from Marina to Badagry and so on and so forth,” he said. “Today, over four million people have the Cowry card. What does that mean? It means you can use ferry, you can use rail, and you can use BRT buses — one payment — so that we can deal with how to subsidise it. On healthcare, the APC candidate promised to expand access to medical services by increasing the number of primary healthcare centres providing round-the-clock services. Hamzat said that out of the over 300 primary healthcare centres, the government planned to increase its flagship PHCs from 87 to 150, with the facilities operating 24 hours a day. He also disclosed that the state government was building more hospitals to improve healthcare access for residents.
